newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee physicals slow, buyers covered.
newsitem.headline: German coffee physicals slow, buyers covered.

text.p: German physical coffee markets remained quiet as consumers postponed buying for autumn dates and beyond, traders said on Monday.
"The European industry is mostly covered for the summer in contrast to United States roasters, who tend to buy quickly and include far more robustas," one said.
"But some traders still appear short," he added.
Origin offers for May/June were thin but Brazil was offering from July onwards at attractive minus differentials.
The ending of a truckers' strike in Colombia last Friday pressured arabica futures but this was partly cancelled out by low stocks and uncertainty over Latin American crop numbers.
Kenyan prices soared because of buying interest and dwindling high quality supply, traders said.
Kenyan arabicas are included in typical German blends and substitutes were hard to locate, with Rwanda and Burundi offers disrupted by ethnic strife.
Zambian, Zimbabwean and South African supplies will only become available from August onwards.
Alternative coffees may also come from Mexico and Papua-New Guinea.
In the import markets, Kenyans cost $350 per 50 kg fob, having gained $48 on the week.
Brazils cost an unchanged $203 basis May/June, Colombians $258, up $3, and Vietnam G-2 was cust $4 to $72, cif basis.
